name: Combination game
description: Scottish school of the late 19th century: the team moves together and passes the ball from foot to foot, against the English individual dribbling game.
phrase: I want the ball to move from foot to foot and the team to move together, not one player carrying it alone.

name: Danubian school
description: The passing game between the wars in Central Europe (Austria, Hungary, Czechoslovakia), with the game built collectively.
phrase: I want every pass and every movement to have a purpose, building the game with the ball on the ground.

name: WM (Chapman)
description: Chapman's formation at Arsenal after the offside change: three defenders, two half-backs and a five-man attack, with quick counter-attacks.
phrase: I want a team that gets results above all, defending with three centre-backs and attacking at speed.

name: Hungarian fluid 4-2-4
description: The Hungarian idea of the late 1940s and 1950s: a deep-lying centre-forward who organises the game and drags the centre-half out of position, with forwards interchanging.
phrase: I want a centre-forward who drops deep to organise the game and forwards who swap positions to unsettle the defence.

name: Kick and rush
description: The British direct tradition: win the ball, get it forward fast with long passes and early crosses, and fight for every second ball, with set pieces as a main weapon.
phrase: I want to win the ball, get it forward quickly and fight for every challenge, using the team's strength.

name: Futebol-arte / jogo bonito
description: Brazilian flair football in which individual talent comes first, against results-based football: beautiful play is the way to win.
phrase: I want the talent of the stars to lead the game, and believe that you can play well and win.

name: La Nuestra / Rioplatense
description: The Río de la Plata tradition of dribbling, short passing and improvisation by small, technical players, the criollo style the writers called 'la nuestra'.
phrase: I want a technical team, built on dribbling and short passing, with its own identity.
